To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of membranes made from blends of PVDF with copolymers containing zwitterionic monomers can be improved by selecting a copolymer that has a zwitterion content in the range of 18 19wt%, and that membranes containing only 5 10wt% of such copolymers can have significantly improved flux and complete fouling resistance to oil and protein suspensions.

the performance of membranes made from blends of PVDF and zwitterionic copolymer additives is highly dependent on the properties of the copolymer additives, and that the best results are achieved with blends that contain a zwitterionic copoymer with 18 19wt% zwitterionic content.

zwitterionic copolymer additives that contain 18-19 wt% of zwitterion monomer are optimal to achieve high flux and complete fouling resistance in PVDF membranes, and the zwitterion monomers sulfobetaine methyl methacrylamide and sulfobetain 2 vinylpyrimidine are more favorable than sulfobetaine vinylpyridine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of zwitterion containing additives for fouling resistance in PVDF membranes.

the development of a new class of zwitterion containing copolymers for use as additives in the manufacture of ultrafiltration membranes from PVDF, with a focus on the impact of copolymer design on membrane performance.
the design and selection of zwitterionic copolymer additives to achieve membranes with high permeance, high fouling resistance and high chemical resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the NIPS process, copolymer additives that contain a low amount of zwitterionic monomers (18 19 wt%) and have high molecular weight (Mw > 100 kDa) can be successfully blended with PVDF to produce membranes with high flux, high selectivity, and excellent resistance to irreversible fou ling.
, in order to attain the best performance, the additive copolymeric should have a composition that is neither too hydrophobic nor too zwitterionic.
the copolymer composition, i.e. the zwitterion/hydrophobic ratio, is the most important factor in the design of zwitterionic copolymer additives for membrane modification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of zwitterionic additive membranes is not only determined by the zwitterion content in the additive, but also by the hydrophobic/hydrophilic balance in the additive copolymers and the additive content in the membrane.

the best performance is achieved when the additive is miscible with PVDF, and when the additive is a copolymer of a hydrophobic monomer and a zwitterionic monomeric group with a low zwitterionic content, typically less than 20 wt%.

, for a given hydrophobic polymer, the best performance can be achieved by blending a small amount of a copolymer with a zwitterion content in the range of 20 wt%, and that this performance is not very sensitive to the zwitterion chemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the copolymer design rules for membrane surface modification by zwitterions are not straightforward.
copolymer additive design is critical for achieving high membrane performance.
, to design a zwitterion additive copolymer for fouling resistance membranes, it is critical to consider its compatibility with PVDF and its ability to segregate to the membrane surface.
